title: Proof of Attraction
tagline: A dating app where real human verification is built into every interaction.
description:
PROOF OF ATTRACTION
Detailed Project Description
ETHOnline 2026 — World Track

===============================================================================
THE ONE-LINE IDEA
===============================================================================

A dating app where every single profile is a verified, unique, living human —
no bots, no catfish, no duplicate or throwaway accounts — and where an optional
human-backed AI agent can act on your behalf in a way the person you are talking
to can actually trust.

Human verification is not a badge bolted on at the end. It is the foundation the
whole product stands on. If you cannot prove you are a real, unique person, you
do not get in.


===============================================================================
THE PROBLEM
===============================================================================

Every mainstream dating app has the same three rotten foundations:

1. Bots and scammers. A large share of "people" on dating apps are automated
   accounts, romance scammers, or paid engagement farms. Users waste time,
   lose money, and lose trust.

2. Fake and duplicate identities. One person can spin up ten profiles. Banned
   users return instantly under a new email. There is no notion of "one real
   human = one account."

3. No trust in AI. AI is flooding these apps — auto-swipers, script-written
   openers, ghost-written conversations. When a message feels too smooth, you
   cannot tell if a human is even involved. AI is treated as something to hide.

The result: matching feels like gambling against machines, and the moment AI
enters the chat, trust collapses entirely.


===============================================================================
THE CORE INSIGHT
===============================================================================

The scarce, valuable thing in online dating is not looks or wit — it is the
guarantee that there is ONE REAL, UNIQUE HUMAN on the other side.

World ID can prove exactly that, anonymously, without collecting your identity
documents or selling your data. So we built a dating app where that proof is the
entry ticket, the trust signal on every screen, and — crucially — the thing that
makes AI safe instead of scary.

Instead of hiding AI, we make it accountable: an agent may act for you, but every
action it takes is cryptographically tied back to a verified human via World's
AgentBook. The other person sees "this was sent by a verified human's agent,"
not "you might be talking to a bot."


===============================================================================
HOW IT WORKS FOR A USER (THE EXPERIENCE)
===============================================================================

1. PROVE YOU ARE HUMAN (onboarding)
   You open the app and verify with World ID. This is a real, anonymous proof of
   personhood — one account per unique human, enforced at the protocol level. No
   email/password, no phone number. The proof itself is your identity.

   Because World ID 4.0 nullifiers are one-time-use, we also create a World ID
   "session" during signup so you can log back in later with a single tap,
   without re-proving from scratch. On a new device you just enter your handle
   and approve the login in the World App.

2. LIVE SELFIE ESTIMATE (optional, clearly labelled)
   A quick two-frame front-camera check. It confirms you are a live person in
   front of the camera (not a photo of a screen) via a small liveness challenge
   — "turn your head", "smile" — and records an ESTIMATED gender presentation.

   This is shown everywhere as an estimate, never as "verified." World does not
   verify gender and we never claim it does. It is a third-party vision-model
   guess, kept honest and separate from the real human-verification badge.

3. BUILD A PROFILE
   Handle, photos, bio, interests, self-declared gender, who you are looking for,
   and location. Photos are stored privately and served through short-lived
   signed links, never as permanent public URLs.

4. DISCOVER REAL HUMANS ONLY
   You swipe through other verified humans. Each card shows a humanity badge
   (Orb / Selfie tier), an "Agent enabled" badge if that person authorized an
   agent, and a compatibility match score computed from shared interests, age,
   distance, verification tier, and on-chain reputation signals. A "Verified
   humans only" filter is always available.

5. THE AGENT ACTS FOR YOU (the AgentKit part)
   You can register a personal agent. It genuinely acts on your behalf:
     - "Ask my agent about her" — pre-screens a profile and gives you a take
       before you even match.
     - Auto-suggested opener — when you match, your agent drafts a first message
       in your chosen tone (warm / witty / direct). You can send via the agent,
       edit it, or dismiss it.
     - Reply drafting — mid-conversation, it drafts your next reply from the
       thread.
   The recipient always sees a disclosure: "sent by a verified human's agent."
   Nothing is hidden.

6. TRUST GATES ON HIGH-STAKES MOMENTS
   First message and event RSVP are the moments abuse actually happens, so
   human-verification is required there — a bot cannot send the first message or
   claim a limited event seat.

7. AN ACTION LOG YOU CONTROL
   Every action your agent takes is recorded and shown to you, each tagged with
   whether it was cryptographically verified through AgentBook. You can revoke
   any action. You always know what your agent did in your name.


===============================================================================
WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT
===============================================================================

- Verification is the product, not a feature. The entire funnel is gated on
  proof of a unique human. This is Sybil resistance applied to dating.

- AI is disclosed and accountable, not hidden. Most apps pretend AI is not
  there. We surface it and make it provably human-backed. That flips AI from a
  trust-destroyer into a trust signal.

- Privacy-preserving by construction. World ID proves personhood without
  revealing who you are. We store an anonymous nullifier, not your identity.

- Gender is handled honestly. It is an ESTIMATE from a live selfie, always
  labelled as such, always separate from the real human badge. We refuse to
  launder a guess as a verified fact.


===============================================================================
THE PRIZE ANGLE (ETHOnline — World Track)
===============================================================================

The build targets both World prizes at once, and they reinforce each other:

- AgentKit Continuity: a human-backed agent acts in chat and discovery, and
  every action routes through a real AgentKit-protected backend that resolves
  the agent to a human through AgentBook on World Chain. A durable, per-human
  free-trial quota (keyed to the verified human, not a device or wallet) demos
  real continuity, with an on-chain testnet top-up when the trial runs out.

- Selfie Check / Proof of Human: human verification is used as a risk,
  eligibility, fairness, continuity, and abuse-prevention signal at the two
  highest-stakes moments — first message and event RSVP — not as a one-time
  checkbox.


===============================================================================
ONE-SENTENCE PITCH
===============================================================================

Proof of Attraction is a dating app where you can finally be certain the person
you match with is a real, unique human — and where AI is allowed to help, but
only when it is provably backed by one.
how_its_made:
PROOF OF ATTRACTION
How It's Made — Deep Technical Description
ETHOnline 2026 — World Track

===============================================================================
1. HIGH-LEVEL ARCHITECTURE
===============================================================================

Three moving parts:

  [ React Native app ]  --HTTPS-->  [ Hono API on Vercel ]  -->  [ Neon Postgres ]
        (Expo)                          (serverless)                (Drizzle ORM)
           |                                |  \--> Upstash Redis (quota/nonces)
           |                                |  \--> AWS S3 (private photos)
           |                                |  \--> Ably (realtime chat)
           |                                |  \--> Groq LLM (OpenAI-compatible)
           |                                |  \--> World Chain (AgentBook, reputation)
           |                                \--> developer.world.org/api/v4/verify
           \--> WebView -> IDKit (World App) for World ID proofs
           \--> Privy embedded wallet + viem for testnet top-ups

- Client: React Native via Expo SDK 57, Expo Router for navigation. Standalone
  app (not a World Mini App), built as an Android dev/release APK.
- Backend: Hono, deployed to Vercel serverless (local dev via @hono/node-server).
  Stable public alias: server-two-steel-51.vercel.app.
- Repo split: /app and /src (client), /server (backend), /docs (submission +
  feedback docs). Drizzle migrations in /server/drizzle.


===============================================================================
2. IDENTITY, AUTH, AND SESSIONS (the hard part)
===============================================================================

There is no "Sign in with World ID" session product — IDKit produces a one-shot
proof, not a session. So we own the session lifecycle.

WORLD ID 4.0 SPECIFICS THAT SHAPED THE DESIGN
- We use idkit-core 4.2.4 and verify against developer.world.org/api/v4/verify/{rp_id}.
- v4 requires a signed rp_context: the backend signs a short-lived request token
  with an RP signing key (signRequest from @worldcoin/idkit-core/signing) before
  the widget can open. App ID + RP ID + signing key are the three portal values.
- v4 uniqueness nullifiers are ONE-TIME per (rp, action). Re-verifying the same
  action returns nullifier_replayed. There is no "max verifications" toggle on a
  v4 action page. This is why naive "verify again to log in" does not work.

THE FLOW WE BUILT
- Signup: proofOfHuman uniqueness proof (Sybil check, action from
  EXPO_PUBLIC_WORLD_ID_ACTION) -> backend verifies -> issues our own HS256 JWT
  keyed to the anonymous nullifier -> upserts a users row. Immediately after, we
  run IDKit.createSession and store the returned session_id on the user
  (users.world_session_id) and in SecureStore.
- Login: IDKit.proveSession(session_id) -> POST /auth/session/prove -> new JWT.
  No uniqueness re-proof, so no replay. On a fresh device with no stored session,
  the user types their handle -> GET /auth/session/lookup?handle= resolves the
  session_id -> proveSession.
- The WebView page (server/public/verify.html) takes a mode param:
  uniqueness | create-session | prove-session, and drives IDKit accordingly.
  A native bridge (WorldIdProvider / WorldIdModal, react-native-webview) returns
  the proof to the app.

TOKEN HANDLING
- JWT (7-day) stored in expo-secure-store, attached as a Bearer token by
  authedFetch, which transparently retries once via POST /auth/refresh on a 401
  before signing out.
- The derived humanId (from the nullifier) is the exact key the AgentKit quota
  counts against — tying agent continuity to the verified human.


===============================================================================
3. THE AGENT — REAL AGENTKIT, NOT A COSMETIC CHATBOT
===============================================================================

What makes it a genuine AgentKit integration: every in-chat/discovery agent
action routes through an AgentKit-protected backend endpoint, and the server
verifies the caller against AgentBook on every call.

CLIENT SIDE (src/agent/agentkit.ts)
- Uses @worldcoin/agentkit createAgentkitClient + declareAgentkitExtension.
- CRITICAL: the extension is declared with network 'eip155:4801' (World Chain
  Sepolia). Without the network, supportedChains is empty and createHeader throws
  "Signer eip155:4801/eip191 is not supported" — the bug that silently dropped to
  the fallback gate. The signer is the Privy embedded wallet (eip191, signMessage).

SERVER SIDE (server/src/agentkit.ts + agentGate in index.ts)
- Real verify path: parseAgentkitHeader -> validateAgentkitMessage (maxAge 300s,
  nonce replay set) -> verifyAgentkitSignature (RPC) -> AgentBook lookupHuman.
- Fallback gate: if no/invalid AgentKit header, resolve via x-agent-wallet against
  a homegrown registry. The response carries a "gate" field: "agentkit" or
  "fallback: <reason>", surfaced in the app ("Last call: agentkit").
- AgentBook is read on World Chain mainnet (eip155:480) — a free eth_call,
  no funds, no tx. Our agent signs on Sepolia (eip155:4801). Single deliberate
  mainnet touch, flagged; the fallback covers it if unavailable.

AGENT ENDPOINTS (all pass through agentGate)
  POST /agent/context     pre-screen a profile or read match context (generateTake
                          for discovery, generateContext for a match)
  POST /agent/icebreaker  draft a first message in a chosen tone
  POST /agent/reply       draft the next reply from the last ~8 messages
  POST /agent/send        send a message as the agent (viaAgent=true)
  GET  /agent/actions     action log + quota { used, freeTrial, credit, remaining }
  DELETE /agent/actions/:id  revoke a logged action

Every call records an agent_actions row (kind, detail, agentBacked, registered),
shown in the Agent tab and revocable.

CONTINUITY QUOTA + x402-STYLE TOP-UP
- FREE_TRIAL_CALLS per verified human, stored in Upstash Redis (durable across
  serverless cold starts). Exhaustion returns HTTP 402 with a top-up target.
- On-chain settlement (testnet only): the agent settles a native ETH transfer on
  World Chain Sepolia (chain id 4801) from the Privy embedded wallet via viem.
  Client reports the tx hash to POST /agent/topup; verifyTopUp
  (server/src/payments.ts) waits for the receipt and checks recipient, minimum
  value, and unused hash (replay protection), then credits N calls in Redis.
- The wallet defaults to World Chain Sepolia (Privy supportedChains) and calls
  wallet_switchEthereumChain to 4801 before sending; the signer pre-checks
  balance to give a clean "wallet has 0 ETH" message instead of a viem stack dump.
- A "Credit from transaction" fallback lets any wallet's tx hash be pasted to
  settle, since a keyless exchange wallet cannot sign on a custom chain.


===============================================================================
4. LIVE SELFIE GENDER ESTIMATE (vision + liveness)
===============================================================================

- Client (src/verification/GenderEstimateCapture.tsx): expo-camera front camera,
  two frames — neutral then a challenge (turn head / smile / raise eyebrows).
  Capture quality is stepped down in a loop until each base64 frame is small
  enough to fit Vercel's ~4.5MB request cap (the FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE issue).
- Server: POST /me/gender-estimate (GET .../challenge issues the challenge).
  llm.ts estimateGenderFromFrames calls a Groq VISION model (qwen/qwen3.6-27b;
  Llama-4 vision is deprecated on Groq) with JSON mode, checking live /
  samePerson / challengePassed plus an estimated label + confidence.
- Result stored in users.gender_estimate. Frames are held in memory only — never
  written to S3 or the DB. Soft signal only: it never blocks, and the profile
  shows a private "estimate differs from what you declared" note, never exposed
  to other users as verified.


===============================================================================
5. DOMAIN MODEL, MATCHING, AND REALTIME
===============================================================================

REPO PATTERN (server/src/repo/{types,memory,pg}.ts)
- getRepo() returns PgRepo when DATABASE_URL is set, else an in-memory MemoryRepo
  (used for local dev and stub mode). Same interface for both.

DRIZZLE SCHEMA (server/src/db/schema.ts)
  users (nullifier_hash, handle, tier, gender_estimate, wallet,
         world_session_id, likes_everyone), profiles, likes, matches, messages,
         events, rsvps, push_tokens, agent_actions.

DOMAIN ROUTES (server/src/routes.ts, all behind requireSession)
  GET  /me                    user + profile (photos presigned)
  PUT  /me/profile            requireOrb
  PUT  /me/handle             unique handle
  POST /me/wallet             link agent wallet -> human
  POST /me/photo              multipart upload
  GET  /discovery             ranked deck (verifiedOnly filter)
  POST /likes                 like/pass, auto-match, push
  GET  /matches, /matches/:id/messages, POST .../messages
  GET  /realtime/token        Ably token
  GET  /events, POST/DELETE /events/:id/rsvp   (RSVP requires human tier)
  POST /push/register

MATCHING (server/src/matching.ts) — pure weighted scorer
  interest Jaccard 0.34, distance (haversine) 0.14, tier 0.14,
  agentBacked 0.14, age 0.12, reputation 0.12; top candidates enriched with
  on-chain reputation signals (onchain.ts: viem publicClient — tx count, balance
  band, AgentBook registration; null-safe).

REALTIME + MEDIA
- Chat over Ably websockets (src/realtime/ably.ts) with a polling fallback and a
  "loaded" flag used to trigger the agent's auto-suggested opener exactly once.
- Photos: private S3 objects (server/src/s3.ts) returned as 12-hour presigned GET
  URLs; blob.ts routes to S3 when configured, else a data-uri/Vercel Blob fallback.
- Push via Expo push tokens.


===============================================================================
6. STACK SUMMARY
===============================================================================

CLIENT
  React Native 0.86 / Expo SDK 57, Expo Router
  @worldcoin/agentkit 0.2.1
  @privy-io/expo 0.73 + viem 2.56 (embedded wallet, testnet signing)
  expo-camera 57 (live selfie), react-native-webview (World ID widget)
  ably 2.28 (chat), expo-secure-store (JWT + session), expo-notifications

BACKEND
  hono 4.6 on Vercel serverless
  @worldcoin/idkit-core 4.2.4 (v4 verify + signing)
  @worldcoin/agentkit 0.2.1 (AgentBook verify)
  drizzle-orm 0.45 + @neondatabase/serverless (Neon Postgres)
  @upstash/redis 1.38 (durable per-human quota + nonces)
  @aws-sdk/client-s3 + s3-request-presigner (private photos)
  ably 2.28 (chat), openai 7.15 -> Groq (LLM text + vision)
  viem 2.56 (World Chain reads + testnet receipt verification)

CHAINS
  World Chain mainnet eip155:480  — AgentBook resolution (read-only eth_call)
  World Chain Sepolia eip155:4801 — agent signing + testnet top-up settlement


===============================================================================
7. NOTABLE ENGINEERING DECISIONS / GOTCHAS SOLVED
===============================================================================

- World ID v4 replay: solved with createSession/proveSession instead of
  re-running uniqueness proofs; login is a session proof, not a new nullifier.
- AgentKit header: must declare the extension on eip155:4801 or createHeader
  rejects the Sepolia signer.
- Vercel payload cap: selfie frames are downscaled client-side until under the
  request limit; non-JSON error bodies (413) are handled instead of JSON.parse.
- Node/undici picks broken IPv6 routes to Neon on some networks; db/client.ts
  forces IPv4 (dns ipv4first + undici Agent family:4), escape hatch NEON_FORCE_IPV4=0.
- Privy provisioning failures were swallowed; useWallet now surfaces the real
  error (e.g. invalid_native_app_id) with a retry, deduped across call sites.
- Everything on-chain is testnet only, never mainnet — the one mainnet touch is a
  free AgentBook read, explicitly flagged, with a fallback gate.
auto_summary: A React Native dating app verifies users with World ID and ties AI messaging agents and wallet-based payments to verified identities.
